topic: Sequence Machine's A322026 Dirichlet-inverse conjecture, final Formula in revision 41 (8 September 2024)
title: Multiplier classifications resolving Sequence Machine's conjecture in OEIS A322026, revision 41, final Formula (8 September 2024): extensions of halasz_resonator's inverse calculation (2026)

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Applying and extending halasz_resonator's inverse calculation (2026, Theorem 4(1)), we prove Sequence Machine's conjecture A322026(n)=A323884(25n), recorded by Antti Karttunen in the final Formula of OEIS A322026, revision 41, 8 September 2024. The rank function a=A322026 is unchanged on multiplying its argument by a prime greater than 3. We show that this invariance forces its Dirichlet inverse b=A323883 to vanish at every multiple of the square of such a prime. We classify all positive multipliers: A323884(Mn)=a(n) for every positive n exactly when gcd(M,6)=1 and M is not squarefree. The same argument proves and extends Karttunen's recorded 2022 identity A126760(n)=A323882(4n). We prove the neighboring rank and ordinal-transform identities and distinguish the smooth-number rank array from the rational rank array in a cross-referenced entry.
summary: Extensions of a prior inverse calculation: all-index proofs of the posed A322026 identity, four complete multiplier classifications, and a corrected smooth-rank identification, with original OEIS attributions.

coverage.lean_statement: For every natural n, a(n)=a(25n)+b(25n), where a is the explicit rank function and b its integer Dirichlet inverse, both extended by zero at n=0.
written_proofs: b(st)=b(s)mu(t) for 3-smooth s and t coprime to 6
neighboring rank, record, counting, mutual ordinal-transform and equality-implication formulas
dual inverse factorization d(st)=mu(s)d(t) and complete multiplier classification for A323882
smooth-rank arrays A247714 and A255975; correction of the A087465 smooth-rank Comment at entry (7,0)
additional_written_proofs: A349135 universal multipliers are exactly powers of 2 at least 4
A323885 universal multipliers are exactly odd nonsquarefree integers
coverage.prior_work: The prime-local mechanism specializes halasz_resonator (2026), Section 3.4, Theorem 4(1); formal prime-variable series are classical (Cashwell and Everett, 1959). OEIS identities retain their original attribution, including Karttunen's 2018 ordinal explanation, 2021 and 2022 dilation identities and 2024 negative A349135 answer.
coverage.finite_checks: Exact-integer comparisons through index 50000; target identity through n=2000; companion 4n and 9n identities through n=12500 and n=5555; all four multiplier classifications for 1<=M<=1000 with explicit witnesses for excluded M; thirteen published prefixes; A349135(72747675)=-14126242; detailed ranges in verification.json.
